title: A limit that is a closed immersion is a closed immersion at a finite stage (closed-immersion transitions)
statement: Let $T$ be a quasi-compact and quasi-separated scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. Let $I$ be a nonempty directed set and $(Z_i)_{i\in I}$ an inverse system of schemes over $T$, with structure morphisms $h_i:Z_i\to T$, whose transition morphisms $Z_{i'}\to Z_i$ ($i'\ge i$) are closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion] (in particular affine [pqf-def-affine-morphism]), and let $Z=\varprojlim_iZ_i$ be its limit [lem-weil-pbc-limit-affine-transition], with $h:Z\to T$ the induced morphism. Assume every $Z_i$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, every $h_i$ is locally of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and $h$ is a closed immersion. Then $h_i$ is a closed immersion for some $i\in I$ (and hence, composing with the closed immersions $Z_{i'}\to Z_i$, for all $i'\ge i$).

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: Take the finite subcover of T.affineCover and let V_a be the affine open ranges. For each V_a the preimage at i0 is affine. Let p_i=h.app i and q=f. Use appLE to identify the projection maps chi_i: sections(p_i^-1 V_a) -> sections(q^-1 V_a); functoriality and the given compatibility give p_i.app V_a followed by chi_i equal to q.app V_a. Equality transport for appLE uses the existing Scheme.Hom.appLE_congr_hom from WeilConjectures.Mathlib.AlgebraicGeometry.Sites.SmallAffineZariski; no duplicate theorem is introduced.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: For fixed V_a, finiteType_appLE produces a finite set s of generators of sections(p_i0^-1 V_a) as an algebra over sections(V_a). Prove by induction on finite subsets t of s that there are a stage j, an affine preimage p_j^-1 V_a, and a surjective comparison rho from the starting stage sections, compatible with the base and limit maps, such that rho(x) lies in the image of p_j.app V_a for each x in t. For t empty, use the starting stage and the identity comparison.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: For the induction step insert x. Surjectivity of q.app V_a lifts chi_i0(x) to a base section r. The difference x-p_i0.app(r) maps to zero in the limit. Push it through the previous comparison rho and cancel the restriction isomorphism to see a section z of the current affine preimage which maps to zero under the unadjusted limit projection. Mathlib exists_app_map_eq_zero_of_isLimit makes z zero after a transition g:j′ -> j. This is the global-section eventual-zero clause applied to the restricted opens limit (the limit-open and global-section nodes below), already bundled in that Mathlib theorem. The new affine preimage is the inverse image under the affine transition. Its section map sigma is surjective by the closed-immersion criterion and the equality of the two preimage opens. Composition rho followed by sigma preserves all compatibility equations. The equality sigma(z)=0 puts the image of x in the base ring image; base compatibility carries the previous lifts forward.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: Apply the finite-subset induction to s. For every element of the starting ring, Algebra.adjoin_induction shows that its image under rho lies in the range of the base ring map: generators lie there by construction, scalars by compatibility, and the range is closed under addition and multiplication. Since rho is surjective, the base ring map at stage j is surjective. Thus for each affine open V_a there is a stage with affine preimage and surjective section map. The same pair of properties persists under every closed-immersion transition, by affine inverse image and composition of surjective section maps.

source.place: Lemma Tag 0A0N (lemma-eventually-closed-immersion, line 956) and its proof (Lemma 09ZM eventually-affine, Morphisms Lemma 01QO closed-immersion)

proof.text: Use IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists on the finite image of the selected stages to choose a common stage i. Every op j with j >= i.unop maps to i and hence to each selected stage, so its preimages of the V_a are affine and its section maps surjective. HasAffineProperty.of_iSup_eq_top for IsClosedImmersion proves h.app(op j) is a closed immersion. Its appTop on a restriction is the section map followed by a presheaf restriction isomorphism. Empty finite covers and empty generating sets are included: IsCofiltered.inf_objs_exists and the empty-set induction require no selected elements.
